p.src: Overview: The final lecture begins by looking beyond the Standard Model toward unification, supersymmetry, and the gauge-hierarchy problem. To see why the Higgs field sits at the center of those questions, we first reconstruct the Dirac Lagrangian and show that a fermion mass mixes left and right chirality. The chiral weak interaction forbids that mass as a bare term; a gauge-invariant Yukawa coupling supplies it only after the Higgs field acquires a vacuum value. We then derive that vacuum value from the Higgs potential, ask why every known elementary mass is tied to this one small scale, and use superconductivity as a physical analog. After the break, the lecture develops renormalization from conductor and dielectric screening, carries the argument into QED and QCD, follows the gauge couplings toward unification, and derives the Planck scale from short-distance gravity. The electroweak scale then returns as the one unexplained small number.

ja: 概観: 最終講義は、標準模型を超えて統一、超対称性、ゲージ階層性問題へと目を向けることから始まる。ヒッグス場がなぜこれらの問いの中心に位置するのかを見るために、まずディラックラグランジアンを再構成し、フェルミオンの質量が左巻きと右巻きのカイラリティを混合することを示す。カイラルな弱い相互作用はその質量を裸の項として禁じる。ゲージ不変な湯川結合は、ヒッグス場が真空期待値を獲得した後に初めてそれを供給する。次にその真空期待値をヒッグスポテンシャルから導出し、なぜ既知のすべての素粒子質量がこの一つの小さなスケールに結びついているのかを問い、超伝導を物理的類推として用いる。対称性の破れの後、講義は伝導体と誘電体の遮蔽から繰り込みを展開し、その議論をQEDとQCDへと運び、ゲージ結合定数を統一へと追い、短距離重力からプランクスケールを導出する。そして電弱スケールが、唯一説明されない小さな数として再び戻ってくる。
zh: 概述: 最后一讲从标准模型之外出发，展望统一、超对称与规范等级问题。为了看清希格斯场为何处于这些问题的中心，我们首先重建狄拉克拉格朗日量，并表明费米子质量混合了左、右手征。手征弱相互作用禁止该质量作为裸项存在；只有希格斯场获得真空值之后，规范不变的汤川耦合才提供质量。随后我们从希格斯势推导出该真空值，追问为何所有已知基本粒子质量都系于这一个小标度，并以超导性作为物理类比。课间休息之后，本讲从导体与电介质屏蔽发展出重整化，把论证带入量子电动力学与量子色动力学，追踪规范耦合走向统一，并从短距离引力推导普朗克标度。电弱标度于是重新作为唯一无法解释的小数出现。

p.src: The Standard Model is not presented here as a closed catalogue. At the start of the evening I want to say where the next course will go. The theory has difficulties rather than logical paradoxes: the gauge hierarchy, the possible role of supersymmetry, and the question of unification. The three gauge factors $SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ describe strong, weak, and hypercharge interactions separately. Could they be subgroups of one larger group? An often studied possibility is $SU(5)$, in which quarks and leptons occupy common multiplets. Whether nature uses that particular construction is a different question. The important clue is that the apparently separate structures fit remarkably neatly into a larger mathematical one.

p.src: The Large Hadron Collider was built in part to expose whatever physics settles these questions. In 2010 its most immediate quarry was the Higgs boson. Finding a Higgs could never mean only adding one particle to a table. A Higgs is identified by an interlocking set of properties: its vacuum value gives masses to the weak vector bosons and fermions, while its fluctuation couples to those same particles with definite strengths. A resonance with the wrong couplings would not be the Standard Model Higgs.  (Editorial clarification: The lecture predates the 2012 discovery. The observed approximately $125\,\mathrm{GeV}$ scalar has, within present precision, the spin, parity, and coupling pattern expected of the Standard Model Higgs. No low-energy supersymmetric particles have been observed as of 2026. These later facts update the historical setting without changing the argument developed in the room.)

この講義は2012年の発見に先立つものである。観測されたおよそ

Moving every term to one side removes the need for an equal sign, prompting the evening’s small mathematical joke: once an equation has been written as an expression that vanishes, the equal sign has done its work.   \left(i\partial_t+i\alpha^i\partial_i-\beta m\right)\psi ,$ with the understanding that a consistent metric convention fixes the relative signs.

p.src:
But the second line of [eq:l10-yukawa-split] is new experimental content. It says that a fermion can emit or absorb a Higgs and, read in the crossed channel, that a Higgs can decay into a fermion-antifermion pair. Schematically, $\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal M(h\to f\bar f)&\propto y_f,
  \\
  \Gamma(h\to f\bar f)
  &=
  N_c\frac{y_f^2m_h}{16\pi}
  \\
  &\quad\times
  \left(1-\frac{4m_f^2}{m_h^2}\right)^{3/2},
\end{aligned}$ at tree level. Here $N_c=3$ for quarks and $1$ for leptons. A larger fermion mass means a larger Yukawa coupling, provided the decay is kinematically allowed. This does not mean every heavy channel dominates: color factors, phase space, loop-induced channels, and decays to vector bosons also matter. It means the fermionic coupling itself is proportional to mass.

p.src: In a superconductor, electrons form weakly bound Cooper pairs. The pair field is schematically an electron bilinear, $\Delta(x)\sim\langle\psi_\downarrow(x)\psi_\uparrow(x)\rangle,$ and carries electric charge $2e$. Static magnetic fields decay over the London penetration depth: $B(x)\propto e^{-x/\lambda_L}.$ The inverse penetration length plays the role of an effective photon mass inside the medium. It is not a vacuum photon mass; it is a property of the superconducting phase.

p.src: Place a positive test charge in an ideal conductor. Its electric field drives mobile negative charge toward it and positive charge away. Current flows until the local source is surrounded by an opposite cloud and no field remains in the bulk outside that cloud; compensating charge is pushed to the remote boundary. A negative source produces the opposite rearrangement. Two dressed sources far apart can then exert essentially no force, even though the charges inserted microscopically were nonzero.

p.src:
At hadronic distances, chromoelectric field lines do not spread spherically like an electromagnetic Coulomb field. Gluon self-interactions squeeze them into a narrow tube between a quark and antiquark. If the tube has approximately fixed energy per unit length $\sigma$, then $V_{q\bar q}(r)
  \simeq
  -\frac{C_F\alpha_s(r)}{r}
  +\sigma r .$ At large $r$, the linear term dominates. Stretching the pair creates more of the tube, like pulling a strand of taffy, and the energy grows rather than tending to zero. This is the confinement side of the story.

p.src: That is where the sequence properly leaves us. The Higgs mechanism has made the Standard Model internally coherent: it preserves the chiral gauge symmetry, gives masses to weak bosons and fermions, and predicts physical Higgs interactions. Renormalization then teaches us how those interactions change with scale and hints that gauge forces may share a unified origin. Gravity supplies a second high scale by an independent argument. None of those successes explains why the Higgs vacuum value is so far below both. The final lecture therefore does not close the subject; it identifies the small number on which the next subject must concentrate.

ja: そこが、この一連の流れが適切に我々を残す場所である。ヒッグス機構は標準模型を内部的に首尾一貫させた。それはカイラルゲージ対称性を保ち、弱ゲージボソンとフェルミオンに質量を与え、物理的なヒッグス相互作用を予言する。次に繰り込みは、それらの相互作用がスケールとともにどのように変化するかを教え、ゲージ力が統一された起源を共有するかもしれないことを示唆する。重力は独立した議論によって第二の高いスケールを供給する。これらの成功のいずれも、ヒッグス真空期待値がなぜ両方よりもはるかに低いのかを説明しない。したがって最終講義は主題を閉じるのではなく、次の主題が集中すべき小さな数を特定する。
zh: 这就是这一序列恰当地留给我们的地方。希格斯机制使标准模型在内部自洽：它保持手征规范对称性，赋予弱规范玻色子和费米子质量，并预言物理的希格斯相互作用。重整化随后教给我们这些相互作用如何随能标变化，并暗示规范力可能有一个统一的起源。引力通过一个独立的论证提供了第二个高能标。这些成功都没有解释为什么希格斯真空期望值远低于两者。因此，最后一讲并没有结束这个主题；它指出了下一个主题必须集中关注的那个小数字。
